plain probe through CLIProxyAPI pinned to the Codex login (temporary alias probe/gpt-6-astra). Hit 2 of 3 at 2.5 minutes and 3 of 3 at 5 minutes, then misses at some later ages (1 of 3 at 30 min, 1 h and 2 h). The published 0 means that there is no tested age through which every check hit, not that this route does not cache. Earlier runs of this route started at 5 minutes, or were made by another client (pi, low reasoning, larger prompts), so this is a first look at 2.5 minutes with plain requests, not a comparison that shows a change. Three window requests of 921,500 tokens went to the same login one to two minutes before the priming, and the owner's own sessions use the login. Early misses also occurred without a large request before the priming and without two models priming at once: GS1 and GA1 (logins-gpt-6-2-2026-11-17, GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra, the same evening) each missed 1 of 3 at 2.5 minutes. That does not rule out every kind of load, and it says nothing certain about the cause of this run's misses, which is not established. The missing session_id is not the cause: CLIProxyAPI copies prompt_cache_key into the upstream session id. CL3 (logins-long-2026-11-17), primed about four hours later with no window request before it, continues this run and is published with it: it missed again, and its data end at 2 h (the proxy refused its 4-, 8- and 12-hour checks, and a restart of the Mac cut it off before 24 h). Served by build ngvoicu-local-e8d8d777 (process of 2026-11-16 18:48:58); its 2-hour checks ran at 14:27 UTC through build ngvoicu-local-a64b6855 (the owner restarted the proxy at 16:18:13 local), every earlier request through e8d8d777. The Codex login answered those checks: from the restart to 16:29:29 its request counter rose by exactly the 6 two-hour checks of LC1 and LC3 and the OpenAI API key by none, and the alias probe/... exists on that login only

probe 0.3.3 through CLIProxyAPI, the request of LC3 with ages out to 24 h (the long schedule plus 24 h). The probe sent prompt_cache_retention "24h" (OpenAI's extended retention, as a client asking for the long cache sends it); CLIProxyAPI deletes it before the Codex login, so the login received the plain request, recorded with no option. Proof: the Codex translator deletes prompt_cache_options and prompt_cache_retention from every OpenAI Responses request (commits 2ab25eae "strip unsupported prompt_cache_options from OpenAI Responses requests", #4915, and 2005788f "filter out prompt_cache_retention in OpenAI->Codex responses request conversion", #5068; codex_executor_request.go: "OAuth and SIWC credentials reject prompt_cache_options, so they keep the translator's removal"), and at 18:23 local the login answered 200 to prompt_cache_retention "bogus-retention" and prompt_cache_options.ttl "bogus-ttl" while it refused an unknown field with 400 "Unsupported parameter" (fields-codex.jsonl). Pinned to the Codex login by a temporary alias probe/gpt-6-astra on that login only (/v1/models?include=accounts lists only the Codex login for it; the plain id also has an OpenAI API key); every answer's X-CPA-AUTH-KIND was oauth, and the OpenAI API key's counter stayed at 0. Served by build ngvoicu-local-c52243ab (process of 18:09:07 local) until the owner restarted the proxy at 18:38:51 local, build ngvoicu-local-4c071f30 (the same plus one commit for the WebSocket auth-kind event, nothing in this request path) after that. Cut off: the 4-, 8- and 12-hour checks were refused by CLIProxyAPI itself (HTTP 400 "unknown provider for model probe/gpt-6-astra"; the owner's configuration of 20:50 local had excluded gpt-6-astra from the Codex login; nothing reached OpenAI), and the Mac was restarted at 10:16 local on 2026-11-18, before the 24-hour check, which ended the run. The run file is the probe's progress file as the restart left it (status "running"), unchanged. A check that errored counts neither warm nor cold, so this run adds data to 2 h only: no data at 4, 8, 12 or 24 h. The published 0 means that there is no tested age through which every check hit, not that this route does not cache. Early misses also occurred without a large request before the priming and without two models priming at once: GS1 and GA1 (logins-gpt-6-2-2026-11-17, GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra) each missed 1 of 3 at 2.5 minutes. That does not rule out every kind of load, and it says nothing certain about the misses of the earlier models. Their cause is not established.
